In this Go codebase (memos), search for:

1. Methods named "Close" across the backend:
- grep -rn "func (.*) Close()" --include="*.go" . | grep -iv test | head -30
- grep -rn "func (.*) Close()" --include="*.go" . | head -40
- grep -rn "\.Close()" --include="*.go" . | grep -iv test | head -40

2. Memo visibility enforcement:
- grep -rn "visibility\|Visibility\|PRIVATE\|PROTECTED\|PUBLIC\|AccessControl\|access.*control\|permission\|canAccess\|isVisible" --include="*.go" . | grep -iv test | head -40
- grep -rn "Visibility" --include="*.go" . | grep -iv test | head -40

3. Data layer entity types:
- grep -rn "type.*struct" --include="*.go" store/ | head -40
- find . -path "*/store/*" -name "*.go" | head -30

4. Memo metadata/snippet:
- grep -rn "snippet\|Snippet\|preview\|Preview\|excerpt\|Excerpt\|payload\|Payload\|property\|Property\|metadata\|Metadata" --include="*.go" . | grep -i memo | grep -iv test | head -30

5. Profile/avatar serving:
- grep -rn "avatar\|Avatar\|profile.*image\|profileImage\|UserAvatar" --include="*.go" . | grep -iv test | head -20
- grep -rn "GetUserAvatar\|ServeAvatar\|avatarHandler\|/avatar" --include="*.go" . | head -20

Report everything.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

Two additional test-only `Close()` methods exist in `/bench/repo/store/test/filter_helpers_test.go` (lines 200 and 282).

**Call chain for shutdown:** `Store.Close()` (line 72 of `store/store.go`) stops all three cache cleanup goroutines (`instanceSettingCache`, `userCache`, `userSettingCache`) and then calls `s.driver.Close()`, which dispatches to the appropriate database driver (SQLite/Postgres/MySQL). The server orchestration in `/bench/repo/server/server.go` calls `s.Store.Close()` (line 146), `s.sseHub.Close()` (line 206), and `s.httpServer.Close()` (line 216).

Notable `.Close()` call sites (non-test, non-generated) include HTTP response body closures in `internal/webhook/webhook.go:156`, `internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go:95`, `internal/storage/s3/s3.go:96`, `internal/httpgetter/image.go:25`, `internal/httpgetter/html_meta.go:145`, email connections in `internal/email/client.go:90,124,168`, file handles in `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` (multiple sites), and `store/deployment_config.go:134`.

## 2. Memo Visibility Enforcement

### The Visibility Type

Defined in `/bench/repo/store/memo.go` (lines 12-22):
```go
type Visibility string
const (
    Public    Visibility = "PUBLIC"
    Protected Visibility = "PROTECTED"
    Private   Visibility = "PRIVATE"
)
```

The protobuf enum lives in `/bench/repo/proto/gen/api/v1/memo_service.pb.go` (lines 28-38) with values `Visibility_PRIVATE` (1), `Visibility_PROTECTED` (2), `Visibility_PUBLIC` (3).

### Enforcement Logic in the gRPC Memo Service

File: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`

**GetMemo (single memo fetch, around lines 44-66):**
- Archived memos are only visible to their creator (lines 44-53).
- If visibility is not `Public`, the request must be authenticated (lines 55-66).
- If visibility is `Private`, only the creator (`memo.CreatorID == user.ID`) can access it; otherwise `PermissionDenied` is returned.

**ListMemos (list queries, around lines 218-227):**
- Anonymous users: `VisibilityList` is set to `[Public]` only.
- Authenticated user querying all creators: a filter is appended -- `creator_id == <userID> || visibility in ["PUBLIC", "PROTECTED"]` -- so the user sees their own memos plus public/protected ones.
- Authenticated user querying another creator specifically: `VisibilityList` is `[Public, Protected]`.

**UpdateMemo (around lines 452-464):**
- When updating visibility, if the memo has a parent (is a comment), the visibility is forced to match the parent memo's visibility.

### Other Visibility Enforcement Points

- **RSS feeds** (`/bench/repo/server/router/rss/rss.go`, lines 90, 141): only `Public` memos are included.
- **Frontend/SEO** (`/bench/repo/server/router/frontend/frontend.go`, line 150): only `Public` memos.
- **File server / attachment access** (`/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go`):
  - Line 677: Public memos on anonymous-allowed instances permit unauthenticated attachment access.
  - Line 699: Private memos restrict attachment access to the creator and admins.
- **Email notifications** (`/bench/repo/server/notification/email.go`, lines 313-316): Private memos suppress notifications; Protected memos get limited detail.
- **User settings**: `MemoVisibility` default is stored in `UserSetting_GeneralSetting` (`proto/gen/api/v1/user_service.pb.go:2996`) and `GeneralUserSetting` (`proto/gen/store/user_setting.pb.go:260`).
- **ACL config** (`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/acl_config.go`): maps public (unauthenticated) endpoints, including `GetUserAvatar` (line 25).

## 4. Memo Metadata / Snippet / Payload

The `Memo` struct (in `/bench/repo/store/memo.go`, line 51) has a `Payload` field of type `*storepb.MemoPayload` (protobuf-generated). The `UpdateMemo` struct also carries an optional `Payload *storepb.MemoPayload` (line 102). The `FindMemoPayload` struct (lines 84-91) supports search by raw content, tags, link presence, task lists, code blocks, and incomplete tasks.

**No "snippet", "preview", or "excerpt" field/concept exists** in the store layer. The memo content is stored as a full `Content string` field.

The gRPC proto layer refers to `LinkMetadata` via `MemoService` methods:
- `/bench/repo/proto/gen/api/v1/memo_service_grpc.pb.go`: `GetLinkMetadata` (line 93) and `BatchGetLinkMetadata` (line 95) -- these fetch metadata for URLs embedded within memos (title, description, image from link targets), not metadata about memos themselves.

## 5. Profile/Avatar Serving

### Avatar Data Model

The `User` struct (`/bench/repo/store/user.go`, line 43) has an `AvatarURL string` field. The `UpdateUser` struct has `AvatarURL *string` (line 58).

In the protobuf API layer (`/bench/repo/proto/gen/api/v1/user_service.pb.go`, lines 248-249), the `User` message has `AvatarUrl string`. The converter in `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_converters.go` (line 36) sets this to `/file/<username>/avatar` when the user has an avatar.

### Avatar Serving Handler

File: `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go`

**Route registration** (line 124):
```go
fileGroup.GET("/users/:identifier/avatar", s.serveUserAvatar)
```

**Handler: `serveUserAvatar`** (lines 167-210):
1. On non-anonymous instances, requires authentication (a valid session, access token, or PAT).
2. Looks up the user by the `:identifier` path parameter (username).
3. Returns 404 if user not found or `AvatarURL` is empty.
4. Parses the avatar as a data URI (format `data:image/png;base64,...`) using `dataURIRegex` (line 98).
5. Validates the MIME type against `avatarAllowedTypes` (lines 74-83): `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/jpg`, `image/gif`, `image/webp`, `image/heic`, `image/heif`.
6. Sets security headers and a `Cache-Control: max-age` header, then returns the decoded binary blob.

**ACL**: The `GetUserAvatar` gRPC method is listed as a public (no-auth-required) endpoint in `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/acl_config.go` (line 25). However, the HTTP file-server handler at `/file/users/:identifier/avatar` does its own auth check based on `s.Profile.AllowAnonymous()`.

### Identity Provider Avatar

The OAuth2 identity provider (`/bench/repo/internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go`, lines 136-138) maps an `AvatarUrl` field from the IdP claims to `userInfo.AvatarURL`. The IdP `FieldMapping` protobuf (`/bench/repo/proto/gen/api/v1/idp_service.pb.go`, line 227, and `/bench/repo/proto/gen/store/idp.pb.go`, line 225) includes an `AvatarUrl` field.
